_about: World nodes for the quest. Each entry becomes a node in a generated
.streamingsector; the sectors are listed in one .streamingblock that the .xl
registers via 'streaming: blocks:'. Four kinds, cheapest first:
markers   worldStaticMarkerNode       an empty named point - what a map pin
points at and what a scene uses as its
origin. No mesh, no entity.
triggers  worldTriggerAreaNode        a volume that notifies the quest graph
on entry. Needs no .ent and no TweakDB
record: 'size' is the half-extent in
metres, so [8,8,4] is 16x16 and 8 tall.
spawners  worldPopulationSpawnerNode  an object the graph switches on later
with questSpawner_NodeType. 'record' is
a TweakDB id. spawnOnStart is always 0.
props     worldEntityNode             an entity template placed in the world.
'template' is a depot path to an .ent -
a vanilla one is fine and costs nothing
to author.
COORDINATE PROVENANCE. Anchors marked 'verified' are teleport targets shipped
by Appearance Menu Mod, so they are known-standable positions in the real world
geometry. Anything marked 'offset' is derived from an anchor by hand and has NOT
been stood on - see OI-9 for how to correct them in game.

_about: Acts 2-4. A ripperdoc clinic in Dogtown, four metres below street level.
This sector used to sit on the Cynosure core at Z -194.78. That coordinate
was real geometry, but it is 275m underground inside the Phantom Liberty
mission space, so the only way in was a teleport. It is now anchored on
vanilla's own ripperdoc shopfront - the prefab is loc_q303_macs_clinic,
dressed by q304 as Farida's - which the player walks into off the street.
Reachability is not inferred from the geometry, it is read out of vanilla:
the sector one level up holds a worldStaticGpsLocationEntranceMarkerNode
named {loc_q303_macs_clinic_gps} at -1891.75 -2486.90 28.00. That node type
exists so the navigation system can route the player to a door on foot, and
there are exactly four of them in the whole of Dogtown. Beside it sits a
worldInteriorAreaNode {q304_Farida_interior_area}, and the front door
(base\gameplay\devices\doors\final\single_door.ent) carries a DoorController
whose authored persistentState is isLocked 0, isSealed 0.
All of that lives in the ordinary streamed Interior/Exterior sectors, not in
a Quest-category one, so it is present whatever the player's PL progress. The
q304_ dressing is not: q304_farida_shop_sign has isVisibleInGame 0 and is
switched on by that mission. The room is permanent, the shop sign is not.

props._zOffset_why: computer_1.ent's origin is NOT at its feet. Its player workspots - personalLinkPlayerWorkspot, ToggleZoomInteraction and personalLinkComponent - sit at local z -1.52, -1.40 and -1.40, and a workspot anchor is where the player STANDS, so this entity expects its origin about 1.5 m above the floor. Vanilla agrees: in quest_73110a178d6e7404 node 12 is at Z 8.705 and the one AI spot on that side of the building (node 4) is at Z 7.221 - a difference of 1.484 m. Placed at the floor point the mesh renders half-sunk and the interaction workspot lands under the floor. 'pos' stays the verified floor coordinate; only the emitted node moves. See D100.

This is 0.25 m behind the front edge of the 1.0 m counter along the NE wall (edge faces heading 225, so yaw 45.0), on its clear stretch past the items in the corner; the stand spot 0.58 m out is open floor.
props._about: The clinic terminal. Here the model is not a placeholder: glue.json's blocked list asks for 'an interactable computer at #ac_clinic_terminal' and this is that computer, the same .ent and appearance vanilla places in quest_73110a178d6e7404.
props._device_why_null: D119. The scene owns the interaction now. Left as a device this prop shows the engine's own Use prompt right beside ash_cache_terminal.scene's hub - two prompts on one screen, and the device one leads to a vanilla computer UI with nothing in it. 'device': null is the documented off switch (D69), and OI-13 answered in game on 2026-09-09 what it leaves behind: the .ent still appears, and cannot be interacted with at all. That is exactly the wanted shape - the model stays, the prompt comes from the scene.
props.scenery: Nothing references this node any more: the prompt is ash_cache_terminal.scene's hub at #ac_terminal_origin, the marker on the same point. Same arrangement as ac_courier_shard.
props._device_status: BACK ON since D70, 2026-09-09. D69 turned this off to bisect a crash against the scene audio events. The bisect ran and returned a verdict the same afternoon: with both buffers off the game still crashed twice inside 15 minutes (16:15 and 16:29), and one of those, signature E4044E73 on redDispatcher10, is the SAME signature this machine threw twice at 11:33 and 11:34 - hours before the buffer existed. Crash rate with the buffer: 2 in 25 min. Without it: 2 in 15 min. The buffer is not distinguishable as a cause, and an inert terminal blocks the quest at its first objective, so it comes back. See D70.
props._device_why: OI-13, answered in game on 2026-09-09: placed with instanceData null this .ent appears and cannot be interacted with at all. The buffer is what carries ComputerControllerPS - isInteractive, and the Devices.Computer record - so a device without one is scenery. reference/device_computer.instancedata.json says where it came from. ac_probe_computer keeps its null buffer on purpose: it is now the control that shows the difference.

_about: D122. Where Mara ends up in the two endings that leave the cache alive.
Markers-only when it is emitted: both props below are 'disabled', because a
body that is only there in some playthroughs cannot be a sector node - a
node is emitted once and cannot be taken out of the world at runtime (the
D118 lesson). source/glue.json draws them instead, keyed on facts, and reads
the pose from HERE so that a corrected coordinate still moves them. That is
the same division ac_splinter_box already uses.
A markers-only sector is also the safest thing this project knows how to
emit: the motel has been markers-only since the beginning and has never
crashed, while the only sector that ever killed the game was the only one
with live props.
THE COORDINATE IS NOT REAL YET. It is the one thing in D122 that cannot be
derived from the game files: 'landfill' appears in TweakDB only as the
attitude group _Landfill_Guards and in the depot only as terrain prefabs
under base\prefabs\environment\terrain\landfill, neither of which carries a
world position. It has to be stood on. Until it is, the map pin and the body
are in the wrong place and nothing else is affected - see 'verified' below.

markers._source: verified - stood on in game 2026-09-18, same capture method as the six echo fragments (D117). Drives three things at once: the map pin on ac_obj_landfill, the 12 m arrival watch in glue.json, and the body itself.

props.disabled_why: Drawn by the glue, not by the sector - it exists only once ashcache_mara_body_placed is 1, which is two of five endings. Kept here because this is where the pose is measured and verified, exactly like ac_splinter_box.
props.scenery: Nothing references this node: there is no prompt on the body and there is not meant to be. Walking inside twelve metres is what the glue watches, and the coroner's note is granted by the graph. Frisking her would be the wrong verb.
props._source: Position verified - stood on in game 2026-09-18, the same point as ac_landfill_body because she IS the marker. Template REPLACED 2026-09-22 (D127) after the D122 one was seen in game and turned out to be a living woman; the one here was read out of the .ent itself rather than inferred from its name - see _about.
props._z_note: No z_offset in glue.json. The captured z is where the player's feet were, which is where a body lying on the ground belongs - unlike ac_splinter_box, which sits on a bench and may still need a nudge.
_about: D127 replaced the D122 template after it was seen in game. The half of that
reasoning that was right is worth keeping: character records named *_dead
ARE ordinary living NPCs - q001_scavenger_dead_man,
q105_jigjig_prostitute_dead and Mara's own base record carry identical
statPools, visualTags, appearanceName and reactionPreset. D122 concluded
from that the corpse had to be in the entity template, and resolved the
raRef hashes to find one. It is not there either.
Read out of the .ent itself (WolvenKit cr2w -s), which is the step D122
skipped: q105_jigjig_prostitute_dead.ent has 110 components, among them
gameAttitudeAgent, gameSquadMemberComponent, gameInventory and
StimBroadcasterComponent, and its eight appearances are every one
service__sexworker_wa_prostitute_poor_0N - living women. It is a complete
NPC puppet. q105 spawns her alive and kills her from quest script. The
deadness was never in any file, only in the quest that used them - which is
why the player found a woman standing on the landfill, unhurt, and crashed
the game by shooting her.
The right object was one directory over, in entities/ rather than
characters/, and CDPR's own word for it is 'fluff' - set dressing.
q105_fluff_dead_body_01.ent has EIGHT components headed by
entCorpseComponent, no AI, no inventory and no health, and exactly one
appearance: wa_q105_fluff_01_corpse. 'wa' is woman-average, so it is a
female body, and there is nothing in it to anger, loot or kill.
The rule this cost twice: a name is a label its author chose. The only
thing that says what a resource IS is the resource. Extract it and read it.
reference/rvc_voices.json says the same about checkpoints.

_alternatives._comment: Two siblings from the same q105 folder, identical in shape and differing only in pose and outfit. Swap the string if 01 lies wrong on the slope. All are real depot paths, all female, all entCorpseComponent.
_alternatives._rejected_base_corpse: base\characters\base_entities\corpse\corpse.ent is real but is a BASE entity the appearance system builds on, not a placeable body.
_alternatives._rejected_mara_alive: ep1\quest\main_quests\q306\characters\q306_fia_undercover_wa.ent is Mara's own entity and has her face, but it is a live NPC - the exact failure D127 is fixing. Her face at the cost of her being alive is not a trade worth making.

props.disabled_why: Drawn by the glue only on the route where V gave her the sidearm. This is the visible half of 'bullet or knife': the gun is on the ground next to her, or there is no gun anywhere.
props.scenery: Nothing references it either - it is the visible half of the wound and no more. The Liberty V is carrying is the item; this is the one she was holding.
props._source: D127 retired the D118 placeholder, which drew a biochip suitcase lying beside the body. int_weapons_002__constitutional_liberty__base1.ent was read out of the archive before it was used: ONE component, entAnimationControllerComponent, no item record, no inventory, no pickup interaction - a weapon-shaped mesh and nothing else, which is the same property that makes the corpse entity safe. It ships ten appearances and defaults to Rogue's engraved one, so the plain one is named; the glue passes it through DynamicEntitySpec.appearanceName. Still not stood on, so verified stays false.
props._offset_note: DERIVED, not stood on, which is why verified stays false. 0.6 m along the right-hand vector of the body's own yaw - right = (cos yaw, sin yaw) at yaw 21.8821 is (0.9280, 0.3726), so the gun lands 0.56 east and 0.22 north of her. Same z: both are on the ground. Its own yaw is the body's plus 90 so the gun lies ACROSS her rather than in line with her, which reads as dropped rather than placed. One measured point, one piece of geometry - if it floats or clips, the fix is here, not in the glue.
props._roll_note: D184. The interactive Liberty's mesh stands upright on its grip at roll 0 - that is how it sits in a hand. Roll 90 lays it on its side; checked live at the landfill 2026-09-26 against pitch 90 (still upright). z 3 cm over the body's so the frame clears the ground.

sectors.disabled_why: Off together with ash_cache_probe_car (D80). Not a suspect on its own - the trigger nodeData is copied from hotfuzz, the one shipped mod whose entire mechanism is a quest trigger - but it goes out in the same cut so that the next launch has no spawner and no trigger left anywhere in the world: six inert marker nodes and nothing else. If the clinic still dies with that archive, no world node can be the cause and the search moves to the questphase and the journal. ac_probe_computer inside it is already off. Nothing here is quest content.
sectors.probe: Not quest content. Two nodes that answer, in one look, whether this project can place an INTERACTABLE object at all - see D15. Its nodes are exempt from the 'defined but nothing references it' check because nothing is SUPPOSED to reference them. Delete this whole sector once OI-13 is closed.
_about: Everything here sits on #ac_clinic_entrance, which is one of the two VERIFIED
coordinates (OI-9), so a node that does not appear failed for its own reasons
and not because it was placed inside a wall.
It is a SEPARATE sector on purpose, and so are the two spawner probes below it.
A malformed node takes its own sector down with it. Splitting them means each
question fails on its own: if this sector is empty but the car sector is not,
the answer is about the .ent, not about the location.

triggers._source: verified - stood on in game 2026-09-03, CET Surveyor capture (markers.txt)
triggers._about: Cheapest possible world node: no .ent, no record, no redscript. If the sector loads at all, this one is almost certainly fine.

props.disabled_why: Off for one test - the clinic bisect, D77. Four fatal crashes have now landed within 1.4 m of each other on the clinic floor (-1899,-2479,24) under three different signatures, and the 02:32 one happened with ash_cache_probe_npc already disabled, so D73's spawner is not the cause. What is left is these three nodes: they are the ONLY worldEntityNodes in the project, they are all the same device master (computers\\computer_1.ent) with instanceData null, the player has confirmed all three are inert scenery with no interaction prompt, and the only sector that has ever killed the game is the only sector that has props. The motel is markers-only and has never crashed. A device master with no ComputerControllerPS is a half-constructed object; that explains the missing prompt and it is the right shape for a job thread reading garbage. One variable: every marker, trigger and spawner stays. If the clinic stops crashing, this node type is the answer to OI-13 and to the crash at once.
props._source: verified - stood on in game 2026-09-03, CET Surveyor capture (markers.txt)
props._about: The whole question, in one node. Vanilla places this exact .ent with this exact appearance in quest_73110a178d6e7404, but WITH a 200-field instanceData buffer; the cover entity two nodes later has instanceData null. This is that .ent with a null buffer. If it appears AND can be interacted with, terminal_read, box_opened and cabinet_opened are all cheap. If it appears but is inert, they need the buffer. If nothing appears, they need a mod-authored .ent.

sectors.disabled_why: Off - and this one is a suspect, not just a bisect step (D80). The clinic crash is ONE instruction, Cyberpunk2077.exe+0x1D173BE / ID 1912746313+0x1E, five fatal logs, the first at 2026-09-09 20:50 and none in the 251 logs before it. The 2026-09-10 12:23 crash reproduced it with every other mod on this install removed - two archives in archive/pc/mod, both ours - so it is our archive. Props were already off for the last three of those five, ash_cache_probe_npc was already off, and the markers are inert worldStaticMarkerNodes with all-zero nodeData that have shipped unchanged for weeks. The one structural change inside the window is this node: it moved from -1916.6,-2467.91,24.06 (buried indoors, where it never spawned anything) to a verified spot on the street outside the clinic on 2026-09-09. It also carries spawnOnStart: 1 where every vanilla quest-content spawner in reference/sectors.md ships 0, and appearanceName default, which is the worldEntityNode prop convention - a Galena appearance is named thorton_galena__basic_*, and a CName that resolves to nothing is exactly the -1 this instruction dereferences. The control it provided is already moot: the FIA agent rendered, so the car decides nothing.
sectors.probe: Not quest content. The control half of the spawner experiment - see D15. Delete with the rest of the probes once OI-13 is closed.

spawners._source: verified - stood on in game 2026-09-06, CET Surveyor capture (ash_cache_debug/markers.txt). Replaces a DERIVED value.
spawners._about: The CONTROL. A Vehicle record is the only kind vanilla ever puts in a spawner node, so if this one does not appear, nothing below it means anything and the problem is the location or the node itself.

sectors.disabled_why: Prime suspect for the clinic crash - see D73. Three fatal crashes on 2026-09-09 landed within 1.4 m of each other on the clinic floor, all a redDispatcher job thread reading 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, and signature 93CABB10 appears twice in those three and in none of the 237 crash logs before them. This spawner sits 3 m from the door the player walks through to get there, and it is the one node in the project doing something no vanilla sector does: a Character record in worldPopulationSpawnerNode.objectRecordId. Off for one test. If the clinic stops killing the game, OI-13 is answered no and this node is the answer.
sectors.probe: Not quest content. Asks whether worldPopulationSpawnerNode.objectRecordId accepts a Character record - see D15 and OI-13. Its own sector so that a 'no' loud enough to invalidate the sector cannot take the control car down with it. Delete with the rest of the probes once OI-13 is closed.

spawners._source: verified - stood on in game 2026-09-03, CET Surveyor capture (markers.txt)
spawners._about: The VARIABLE, and the whole reason this sector exists. Every objectRecordId in all 698 vanilla quest sectors is a Vehicle.*; not one is a Character.*, because vanilla spawns NPC groups from communities instead. So whether a spawner node accepts a Character record is a guess, and it is the last thing standing between cleanup_done and being authorable. q305_fia_agent is a real Phantom Liberty FIA agent, which is who the cleanup crew would be, so a yes here is the real content and not just an answer.
